Asha — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front so your teams can act:

- NVMe vs block: we'll use local NVMe for the inference-cache tier only (ephemeral, not for long-term state). All model artifacts and persistent state will mount from CSI block volumes (rbd/iscsi or our preferred CSI driver) behind the site SAN.
- Egress: Redwood prefers a dedicated NAT appliance per rack for predictable egress measurements; we can fall back to routed upstream if your network ops prefers that. No mandatory BGP for initial bring-up — BGP is optional for multi-rack setups.
- KMS: we use TLS over outbound port 443 for KMS provisioning. We'll provide the allowlist CIDRs and the short provisioning runbook by EOD tomorrow.

Irene / Marissa — tagging you for the technical details on nodepools and PV binding behavior. Irene, can you confirm recommended node classifications, eviction behavior, and PVC reclaim policy for a 3-rack private deployment?

Hi Asha / team — detailed technical guidance below. I pulled this together to make the on-site install and ops handoff as low-friction as possible.

Summary recommendations (three node pools):
- inference-gpu (3 nodes per rack, tainted for GPU workloads): local NVMe used only for KV/prefetch cache. PVCs should be of StorageClass: local-ephemeral (ReclaimPolicy: Delete, volumeBindingMode: Immediate) and CSIDriver: local.csi.redwood.
- system-mgmt (2 nodes per rack, no GPUs): hosts kube-system, logging/monitoring agents, and CSI controller. CSI block volumes attached from SAN (StorageClass: site-block, volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer).
- batch-worker (optional, 1–2 nodes rack-level): CPU-only for batch evals/backups, use site-block or NFS for archive.

PVC/eviction behavior:
- Set PodDisruptionBudget for inference-daemonsets to allow 1 pod eviction per rack during maintenance. For cache nodes, use emptyDir backed by NVMe with a short TTL: on reboot the cache repopulates; persistent model data should never be on local NVMe.
- For CSI block volumes, use volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer so PVCs bind to the correct zone (rack). That prevents cross-rack attach failures.

Networking and routing notes:
- MTU: set 9000 across the rack fabric if possible — we observe 5–8% throughput improvement for model pulls.
- Egress: if you provide a dedicated NAT appliance per rack, Redwood will configure SNAT with our observability tags. If upstream routing is used instead, we'll need a static route to the Redwood control-plane endpoints and a planned window to validate egress metrics.
- Optional BGP: recommended only if you plan multi-rack failover with active-active egress. Otherwise static routes are simpler.

KMS/HSM and security:
- KMS provisioning uses outbound 443 over TLS; we will list the ephemeral provisioning IPs. For subsequent key operations we prefer the HSM be reachable via a private link or IP allowlist.
- Audit logs: Redwood can stream node-level audit logs to your SIEM over TLS; please share the endpoint and cert thumbprint for us to configure.

Attachments: I've updated the rack-assignments.xlsx with nodepool mapping (sheet "redwood-mapping"). Also added a one-page runbook snippet in the last tab describing expected node eviction behavior for handoff engineers.

Action items for Novacore site team before handoff:
- Confirm whether rack-level NAT or upstream routing.
- Provide cross-connect VLAN IDs and MTU policy.
- Share KMS allowlist CIDR and SIEM endpoint for audit log integration.

I can join the on-site window for the initial 90 minutes remotely to validate CSI mounts and NVMe health if you'd like.

Cheers,
Irene Choi
On-prem Solutions, Redwood Inference

Asha — closing loop from Redwood ops side and listing firm action items so your ops checklist can consume them directly: 

1) Maintenance window: confirmed Tue 22 Jun 00:30–04:30 local. Redwood will require a 60-minute firmware/BIOS verification window at 00:30 and a subsequent 90-minute validation window for CSI mounts and node health.
2) NVMe/Block mapping: see attached updated rack-assignments.xlsx (sheet: redwood-mapping). Local NVMe = inference cache only. All persistent PVs use site-block StorageClass (vCenter/RBD-backed).
3) Cert rotation guidance: we support a staged rotation flow: short-lived node certs (30 days) with auto-renew using the control-plane endpoint over TLS. For restricted outbound sites we provide an offline CSR workflow (document link in related_links).
4) PVC attach limits: our CSI driver accepts up to 20 concurrent attach/detach ops per node; during restarts we recommend staggered pod restarts using the PDBs Irene suggested to avoid hitting attach throttle.
5) KMS/HSM allowlist: pending your CIDR; Redwood will not initiate any inbound connections.

- Mon 21 Jun EOD: Novacore to provide VLAN IDs, NAT CIDR, and cross-connect ticket.
- Tue 22 Jun 00:30: on-site power & firmware check (Redwood and Novacore remote).
- Tue 22 Jun 01:30–03:00: CSI mount validation and model artifact sync test.
- Tue 22 Jun 03:00–04:30: smoke tests and final sign-off.

Irene and I will be on the call for the entire window. Jonas will handle the initial control-plane validation. Please confirm the cross-connect details when available and we'll add the DocuSign SOW stamp once your facilities team signs off.
